source.label: Sign criteria for the logarithmic derivative of a finite configuration

reviewer: Claude Code proof assessment; fresh medium reviewer

claims.summary: For a nonempty finite multiset R with Phi(s) = sum m_rho/(s - rho): all Re rho <= sigma_0 iff Re Phi > 0 on Re s > sigma_0. For real points Gamma and one conjugate pair gamma +- i delta of multiplicity m, the Laguerre expression L(x) = sum m_w/(x - w)^2 on the real line is negative at x = gamma iff sum over Gamma of m'/(gamma - gamma')^2 < 2m/delta^2, the pair's term is at least -2m/delta^2 and negative only for |x - gamma| < delta, and L >= 0 everywhere when the real points have gaps at most 2 delta/sqrt(m) covering (gamma - delta, gamma + delta).
claims.assessment: Working elementary proofs. The half-plane sign criterion is equivalent to the zero-free statement at every boundary, so it is not a weaker premise; the local real-line (Laguerre, phase-monotonicity) condition cannot fail for an off-line pair farther from the line than half the gap of the real points around it times sqrt(m), while the global count of real zeros detects every pair and is the goal's statement. Finite configurations only; part (a) is the finite model of a known equivalence and no novelty is claimed; the general Hermite-Biehler and de Branges sources are not read.
claims.rationale: Shows for finite configurations that the Hermite-Biehler lead's two natural forms are the goal's statement and a criterion blind in the relevant range.
claims.next_action: Read a source on structure functions of de Branges type for xi and state which condition is equivalent to the goal and what is known unconditionally.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

notes.mathematical_status: Complete proofs in the entry; no computation.
notes.significance: Context: elementary and classical in substance (Laguerre inequality). Novelty not claimed.
notes.relationships: Compared with extreme eigenvalue detection, whose range of detected distances is complementary.

relationships: The local real-line condition can fail only for pairs nearer than the local gap; the Gram form's extreme eigenvalues are proved to see pairs farther than about loglog T/log T; between the scales neither gives detection.
